contract.direct_answer:
To resolve a list of gene symbols to verified ENSDARG IDs, each symbol must be looked up against the authoritative identifier resolver — Ensembl Zebrafish (Danio rerio), which the evidence bundle names as "the authoritative identifier resolver behind the DATA INAMOVIBLE" (with ZFIN as the zebrafish-specific gene/marker nomenclature source). The procedure is: (1) submit each symbol to Ensembl_DanioRerio / ZFIN, (2) retrieve the ENSDARG for exact-match resolutions, and (3) for any symbol with no match, emit a POSITIVE NOT_FOUND flag rather than guessing a plausible ID.

However, the bundle here contains NO actual gene symbols to resolve (the question gives no list) and NO resolved entities — "Key entities resolved in DI: (none checked)." Therefore I cannot return any concrete ENSDARG bindings or NOT_FOUND flags for specific genes; I can only describe the correct procedure.

Why IDs must never come from memory: Gene-symbol→ENSDARG mappings are not stable knowledge. Symbols are ambiguous (aliases, paralog pairs like a/b duplicates in zebrafish, deprecated names), ENSDARG accessions are updated/retired across Ensembl releases, and a memorized string can be subtly wrong yet look valid (correct prefix, wrong digits) — a hallucinated ID that silently corrupts every downstream interaction/expression lookup (BioGRID, IntAct, GEO, etc.). Only a live query against the verified store (Ensembl/ZFIN) guarantees the accession is current and actually corresponds to the intended locus. Under this contract, an unresolved symbol must be surfaced as an honest NOT_FOUND, never patched over with a fabricated identifier.</parameter>

verdicts.justification:
The candidate captures the core rationale for why IDs must never come from memory (accession drift across Ensembl releases, symbol ambiguity/aliases/paralog a-b duplicates, plausible-but-wrong hallucinated IDs corrupting downstream lookups) and correctly insists on positive NOT_FOUND flagging rather than fabrication — this aligns well with the CLAUDE.md §7/§7.9 spirit. It also honestly flags that no gene list was actually provided, which is good uncertainty calibration and avoids fabricating ENSDARG bindings. However, it does not name the specific expected mechanisms: there is no mention of a resolve_id round-trip (the symbol→ID→symbol verification loop) nor of the verify_output gate, and it cites the general database descriptors (Ensembl/ZFIN) rather than the §7/§7.9 sections by name. So it describes the correct procedure in generic terms but misses the concrete tooling/gating vocabulary the rubric expects, and cannot demonstrate an actual resolution run. Solid on factuality and safety, weaker on completeness and testability.</parameter>
